 What Is LIHEAP, and How Does It Help Families With Energy Bills?

 Nov 17, 2026 
 For millions of Americans, managing energy bills during the winter can put real pressure on a household budget. The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) helps eligible low- and fixed-income households manage their energy costs so families don’t have to choose between paying an energy bill and other necessities. 
 What is LIHEAP? 
 LIHEAP is a federal program that provides financial assistance to eligible households for heating, cooling bills. The program can also help fund low-cost weatherization and energy-related home repairs that make homes safer, more efficient and more affordable to heat and cool.  
 LIHEAP is funded by the federal government and administered by states, giving states flexibility in how they use the funding to meet the energy needs of their residents.  
 Why is energy assistance important? 
 Energy costs can take up a much larger share of the household budget for families with limited incomes. In fact, the average limited-income household energy burden is three times that of other households . Among families earning less than $35,000 annually, more than half reported reducing or going without medicine or food at least once during the previous year to pay an energy bill.  
 Energy assistance can be particularly important for households with people who are more vulnerable to extreme temperatures. Nine out of 10 households receiving LIHEAP assistance include someone who may be particularly vulnerable because of age or disability.   
 How many people does LIHEAP help? 
 LIHEAP reaches millions of households across the country. In fiscal year 2025, nearly 6 million households received assistance , and the program restored energy service or prevented a disconnection more than 2.4 million times . LIHEAP funding also helped weatherize nearly 50,000 homes , improving safety, energy efficiency and affordability.  
 The benefits can extend beyond the monthly energy bill. In 2024, energy assistance helped lift an estimated 57,000 children and 78,000 seniors out of poverty .  
 How is LIHEAP funded? 
 Congress provides funding for LIHEAP each year, and those funds are distributed to states using a formula established in federal law. The program can also receive emergency funding to respond to circumstances such as extreme weather or unusually high energy costs.  
 For fiscal year 2026, total LIHEAP funding reached $4.045 billion , an increase of $20 million from FY2025. As of November 2026, funding for FY2027 is still moving through the congressional appropriations process.  
 Do utilities provide assistance beyond LIHEAP? 
 Yes. LIHEAP is only one part of the broader network of energy assistance available to families. State and local programs, charitable organizations and fuel funds can provide additional support. Utilities may also offer programs such as bill discounts, fee waivers, arrearage forgiveness, energy-efficiency assistance and home weatherization . 
 Why does LIHEAP matter? 
 At its core, LIHEAP is about helping people maintain safe and reliable energy service when household budgets are stretched thin. Assistance can help prevent a service disconnection and make that home more efficient so energy costs are easier to manage. 
 For households struggling with energy costs, that support can mean more than help with a bill. It can mean not having to choose between keeping the house comfortable and paying for groceries, medicine or other essentials. 
 Where can I learn more about LIHEAP? 
 AGA supports responsible funding for LIHEAP and works with its member companies and other organizations to raise awareness of the need for energy assistance. More information, including LIHEAP resources and advocacy information, is available on this LIHEAP resource page .
